questions.q: "Shuttering" means the same as:
questions.n: Shuttering is the mold for wet concrete.

questions.q: The simplest way to keep fresh concrete moist is:
questions.n: Sprinkling with water is the most basic curing method.

questions.q: A dry stockpile of free-flowing sand naturally slopes at about:
questions.n: Dry sand's angle of repose is around 30–35°; angular crushed gravel stands steeper, around 45°.

questions.q: Shotcrete should be moist-cured for at least:
questions.n: Thin sprayed layers dry fast and need a week of moisture.

questions.q: Which concrete handling practice is NOT allowed under the NSCP?
o: Conveying it in ways that prevent segregation
Remixing concrete that has already set with fresh concrete and placing it
Using equipment that gives near-continuous flow
questions.n: Set concrete must be discarded.

questions.q: G 3/8 gravel falls in which size range?
questions.n: 3/8" gravel is about 6–10 mm.

questions.q: Setting time is counted from the moment:
o: Gravel and cement are mixed dry
questions.n: Hydration and setting start when water is added.

questions.q: Sprayed concrete is also called:
questions.n: Gunite or shotcrete is pneumatically applied.

questions.q: The main job of aggregate in concrete is to:
questions.n: Inert filler cuts paste volume, so less shrinkage and cost.

questions.q: Which formwork stays in permanently, works compositely with the slab, and can allow a thinner slab?
questions.n: Steel decking is left in place and acts as both form and tension reinforcement.

questions.q: Cutting the curing of an RC beam down to 3 days will most likely:
o: Cause shrinkage cracking and lower strength
questions.n: Early drying stops hydration and causes cracks.

questions.q: Lean concrete has less ______ than structural mixes.
questions.n: Lower cement content means low strength, which suits blinding and fill.

questions.q: Class A concrete is proportioned (cement : sand : gravel) at:
questions.n: Class A is 1:2:4. Class AA is 1:1.5:3, B is 1:2.5:5, C is 1:3:6.

questions.q: Self-leveling mortar is mainly used as:
questions.n: It flows into a flat base for floor finishes.

questions.q: Heavily loaded columns and girders are specified as Class AA. Which mix is that?
questions.n: Class AA is the richest common mix at 1:1.5:3.

questions.q: Concrete reaches its specified design strength at:
questions.n: f'c is specified at 28 days.

questions.q: Lean concrete for sidewalks, footpaths and blinding is usually class:
questions.n: Class D is the leanest standard class.

questions.q: Loading a one-bagger mixer, the crew follows the usual sequence: part of the water, then...
questions.n: Coarse aggregate first scours the drum, sand next, cement last to avoid balling.

questions.q: Any ingredient other than water, aggregate and cement added to modify concrete is an:
questions.n: Retarders, plasticizers and pozzolans are all admixtures.

questions.q: The slump cone test is mainly an indicator of:
questions.n: Slump measures how fluid the fresh mix is.

questions.q: Beam soffit forms are typically struck at about:
questions.n: Beam bottoms carry more load, so they stay about a week.

questions.q: Screened sand with a uniform grain, preferred for plastering and finishing, is sold as:
questions.n: Vibrosand is screened to a consistent grain for smooth plaster work.

questions.q: Which curing period matters most for strength and durability?
questions.n: Early hydration does most of the work; keep it moist through the first 7 days.

questions.q: Fly ash, silica fume, slag and rice-husk ash are:
questions.n: They react with lime to add binding compounds.

questions.q: Class B concrete is usually taken as about:
questions.n: Class B is around 3,000 psi in common local practice.

questions.q: Which sand should stay out of reinforced concrete?
questions.n: Salt in beach sand corrodes the reinforcement.

questions.q: Ordinary concrete is designed to reach its specified strength at 28 days. Commercial fast-curing ready-mix may get there in about:
questions.n: High-early mixes reach design strength in roughly 7–14 days instead of 28.

questions.q: Crushed angular gravel heaped dry stands at an angle of repose of roughly:
questions.n: Angular particles interlock, so crushed stone piles stand steeper than sand, about 45°.
